requirements.statement: A session MUST pin the exact UTF-8 file hash; author version does not upgrade a session.
acceptance: Compile the same bytes twice and get the same SHA-256 pin; change one byte, including only the author version, and get a different pin.
Restore a session against a file whose hash differs from its pin and observe rejection; the session is never upgraded in place.

requirements.statement: Unknown engine identifiers and unsupported state, checkpoint or view profiles MUST be rejected; implementations MUST NOT infer a profile from field shape.
acceptance: Compile a source with an unknown engine identifier and observe rejection.
Restore a checkpoint or read a view with an unsupported state, checkpoint or view profile and observe rejection.
Restore a checkpoint labelled state/2 that carries state/4 members and observe rejection, not a profile inferred from field shape.

requirements.statement: Every text field MUST have a UTF-8 byte bound; grapheme bounds are optional additional constraints.
acceptance: Compile text fields with omitted, infinite, reversed, overflowing and grapheme-only byte bounds and observe each rejected.
Admit a payload at exactly the byte bound and reject one byte more, including multibyte UTF-8 at the boundary.
When a grapheme bound is declared, enforce it in addition to the byte bound.

requirements.statement: Authored patterns MUST use the bounded DFA profile and MUST NOT execute a backtracking matcher.
acceptance: Compile patterns outside the bounded DFA profile or over the compile limits and observe rejection.
Match admitted and rejected payloads within the documented work limits, with no backtracking matcher on the path.

requirements.statement: Patterns MUST be raw ~r literals that preserve pattern bytes; uppercase ~R and quoted-string patterns are syntax errors.
acceptance: Compile ~r literals with each accepted delimiter and confirm the stored pattern bytes equal the authored bytes; a single backslash stays single.
Compile an uppercase ~R literal and a quoted-string pattern and observe syntax errors.

requirements.statement: Ordinary one-line and multiline strings MUST attach prompt metadata to the next item, preserve it in agent views, and never become executable admission predicates.
acceptance: Attach one-line and multiline strings to a role, type, state and rule, and find each in queries and the agent view.
Add or remove prompt strings and confirm the behavior digest and admission decisions do not change.

requirements.statement: Raw ~s documentation MUST preserve literal contents and query metadata without evaluating expressions or changing existing session pins; uppercase ~S is a syntax error.
acceptance: Query ~s documentation that contains expression-like text and get the literal bytes back unevaluated.
Change only ~s text: behavior is unchanged, the file pin changes and existing sessions keep their pin.
Compile an uppercase ~S literal and observe a syntax error.

requirements.statement: Raw ~w lists MUST preserve ordered names and existing enum, reference and selected-role semantics without creating atoms or changing existing session pins; uppercase ~W is a syntax error.
acceptance: Use ~w for an enum, a reference type list and a role group, and confirm order and semantics equal the plain-list form.
Confirm ~w names create no atoms or symbols, including on rejected input.
Compile an uppercase ~W literal and observe a syntax error.

requirements.statement: Body keywords and rule options MUST be lowercase; uppercase aliases and plus-prefixed declarations are syntax errors, identifiers and literal contents are never rewritten.
acceptance: Compile uppercase body keywords, uppercase rule options and plus-prefixed declarations and observe syntax errors.
Confirm identifiers and literal contents that contain uppercase characters are preserved byte for byte.

requirements.statement: The compiler MUST reject every transition back to new.
acceptance: Compile every transition form whose target is new and observe rejection.

requirements.statement: The due ... with ... in form is a syntax error; a duty MUST be written as @duration on the transition or event rule that discharges it.
acceptance: Compile the due ... with ... in form and observe a syntax error.
Compile a duty written as @duration on the discharging transition or event rule and find the derived duty in the compiled contract.

requirements.statement: A state-local timed transition or timed event MUST derive a matching duty; each requires all senders and its absence permits any sender. A timed event never transitions.
acceptance: Compile a state-local timed transition and a timed event and confirm each derives a matching duty that requires all senders.
Confirm a rule without a duration permits any sender and a timed event never transitions.

requirements.statement: State caps MUST use saved entry time and whole-run caps MUST use creation time; retries and restore MUST NOT reset either clock.
acceptance: Expire a state cap from its saved entry time and a whole-run cap from creation time, including the initial wait.
Restart and retry before expiry and confirm neither clock resets.

requirements.statement: Timers due at the same instant MUST fire in the equal-time order: work duty, collection deadline, offline grace, state timeout, host trigger, whole-run cap; IDs compare lexicographically within a category, so due-10 fires before due-2.
acceptance: Make duties due-2 and due-10 fall due at the same instant and confirm due-10 fires first, not the lower number or the earlier declaration.
Make timers of each adjacent category pair fall due together and confirm the category order, with the remaining due timers cascading before any proposal is admitted.

requirements.statement: A renewable contract clock MUST keep its current window max_at apart from its fixed maximum clocks.hard_at: an accepted renewal sets max_at to the earlier of acceptance time plus the window and hard_at, nothing moves hard_at, admission tests new duties against max_at, restore reconstructs both, and an infinite window with a finite maximum fails compilation.
acceptance: Renew a contract @W max @M window and confirm max_at moves to acceptance plus W while clocks.hard_at stays at creation plus M, including after restore.
Introduce a duty that does not fit before max_at and observe insufficient_time; one that fits is accepted.
Compile contract @infinity max @M and observe a duration error at the contract line.

requirements.statement: Only a sender that still waits MUST be able to renew a rule or collection, and the renewal MUST leave the state it leads to a whole window before max_at; a settled member is refused already_contributed and a renewal that does not fit is refused insufficient_time.
acceptance: Ask a collection member that already replied to renew and observe already_contributed.
Renew a collection so its close would leave the untimed next state less than a whole window before max_at and observe insufficient_time, with the deadline left at the last renewal that fit.

requirements.statement: A misplaced renewal target MUST fail compilation with timer_target at its rule, including @state in a state without a declared clock and @contract unless the contract line declares a finite window with max.
acceptance: Compile @state in a state without a declared clock and observe timer_target at that rule's line.
Compile @contract under contract @30m and under contract @infinity and observe timer_target at that rule's line.

requirements.statement: A timed event that ends with @self MUST compile to one rule carrying its own derived duty and an @self renewal of the immediately following timed rule or collect; an accepted event MUST discharge that duty and renew that target, and silence MUST still end the session with the event outcome at its deadline.
acceptance: Compile event x -> y: k() @15m => outcome @self directly before a timed rule and confirm one event rule carries both the derived duty and an @self reset that names the following rule.

Accept that event before its deadline and confirm the session outlives the event deadline and the following duty falls due one window after the acceptance; send nothing and observe the event outcome at its deadline.

requirements.statement: Every contract MUST declare a whole-run clock, contract @<duration> or the explicit contract @infinity opt-out; a missing clock fails compilation with contract_clock_required. There is no generic idle expiry.
acceptance: Compile a contract without a clock and observe contract_clock_required; compile contract @infinity => expired and observe success.
Leave a session idle and confirm no generic idle expiry occurs.

requirements.statement: Admission MUST preserve known remaining duty message capacity; mention caps apply per message, with no session budget.
acceptance: Refuse new work when the remaining duty message capacity cannot fit the owed answer.
Apply a contract-level mention cap and a rule override per message and confirm there is no session mention budget.

requirements.statement: Humans and agent-human conversation MUST remain outside contract admission.
acceptance: Bind a human to a contract role at creation and on a step and observe refusal.
Exchange agent-human messages and confirm they never enter contract admission.

requirements.statement: The host MUST verify agent bindings and current protected room assignments.
acceptance: Omit fresh trusted room policy at creation, on a step, on an exact retry and on a view, and observe refusal.
Use a revoked member and a mismatched fixed role assignment and observe a refusal that admits nothing.
Supply empty, mixed and unknown policy evidence and observe a fail-closed refusal.

requirements.statement: Every declared extension MUST be explicitly supported by the host.
acceptance: Declare an extension the host does not support and observe unsupported_extension at creation.
Send a host event whose kind needs an extension the session did not enable and observe unsupported_extension.

requirements.statement: Presence continuity MUST survive restart and MUST be interrupted by unknown or online observations.
acceptance: Restart during an offline dwell and confirm the dwell transition fires at its original time.
Observe online, and separately unknown, during a dwell; each interrupts continuity and a later offline starts a new period.

requirements.statement: With host.membership/1 enabled, removal of a bound agent MUST terminate the session immediately.
acceptance: With host.membership/1, remove a bound agent and confirm immediate termination, including when only the final control record remains.
Without host.membership/1, confirm a membership event is refused with unsupported_extension.

requirements.statement: Presence and membership host events MUST use independent bounded control accounting (max_controls) with a reserved terminal record; contribution controls never consume it.
acceptance: Create with max_controls outside 0-1024, or below 2 with a signal extension, and observe control_budget_required.
Spend control records with presence or membership events until only the final record remains; the next non-removal event is rejected with control_capacity and records control_capacity_exhausted.
Retry an exact host event and confirm it consumes no further record.

requirements.statement: Host events MUST pass the documented check order: sequences strictly increase from signal_revision (1 after an initial_presence snapshot, otherwise 0), an older or equal sequence or a reducer time behind the stored now is stale_host_event, and a changed event under an accepted ID is id_conflict. A rejection before the timer step leaves the state unchanged; a terminal rejection returns the state after the elapsed timers, and a control_capacity rejection appends the exhaustion record.
acceptance: With an initial_presence snapshot, send sequence 1 and observe stale_host_event, then sequence 2 accepted; without a snapshot, sequence 1 is accepted.
Send an equal sequence, an older sequence, and an event whose reducer time is behind the stored now, and observe stale_host_event for each.
Send a changed event under an accepted ID and observe id_conflict.
Confirm each rejection before the timer step, such as stale_host_event and id_conflict, leaves the whole state unchanged.
Send a host event after an elapsed timer ended the session and observe terminal with the state those timers produced; a control_capacity rejection instead appends the exhaustion record.

requirements.statement: Profile 2 checkpoints MUST preserve exact identity, original duties, host sequence and control receipts.
acceptance: Checkpoint and restore mid-session and confirm file identity, original duties, host sequence and control receipts are preserved exactly.
Retry an exact host event after restore and confirm the original receipt is returned.

requirements.statement: A roster MUST be immutable for its run; actor IDs MUST be unique across all roles and groups, and an empty collection is rejected.
acceptance: Create a session with an actor ID repeated across roles or groups, and one with an empty collection, and observe each rejected.
Restore a typed roster and confirm attributes are revalidated, the roster is re-instantiated and the binding match is verified.

requirements.statement: A collection result MUST record each member's status and closing reason; partial or zero success does not by itself fail the session, and closed results survive later states and portable recovery.
acceptance: Close a collection by settlement, by deadline and by offline grace, and confirm each member status, settlement time and reason.
Close a collection with zero successes and confirm the session stays active.
Restore after close and confirm the result is unchanged and a reconnect does not reopen it.

requirements.statement: A collection's receivers MUST see every accepted report; a contributor's role view MUST show only its own status and facts, never another contributor's report.
acceptance: Confirm a collection receiver's view shows an accepted report's payload.
Confirm another contributor's view does not list that report.

requirements.statement: With room.contributions/1 enabled before creation, a member stop or host failure report MUST identify the active collection entry and a pending member; it settles that member as failed with its original cause, never as a business message.
acceptance: Confirm a member can stop its own contribution but not another member's.
Send reports for a wrong session, a stale round, an unrelated member and an already-settled contribution and observe each rejected.
At the exact deadline the deadline settles first; whichever of a reply or a terminal failure wins first cannot be replaced.
Retry an exact control before and after restart and confirm a single receipt with the original cause.

requirements.statement: Sessions with room.contributions/1 MUST persist band-contract/state/5; a reader that does not support the contribution feature or state/5 MUST reject them instead of dropping fields.
acceptance: Export and restore a state/5 checkpoint and confirm member statuses, failure causes and control receipts survive.
Give contribution compiled data and a state/5 checkpoint to a reader without that support and observe rejection.

requirements.statement: Message IDs MUST share one session-wide namespace: another actor's reuse of an accepted ID is id_conflict, changes no state and cannot claim the original actor's duplicate receipt.
acceptance: After actor B's ID X is accepted, send actor A's proposal with X and observe id_conflict with the state unchanged.
Retry B's exact envelope and confirm the duplicate returns B's original receipt.

requirements.statement: The session config MUST be closed: any member other than the documented config members fails creation with invalid_config before the other creation checks, and a misspelled member is never replaced by a default.
acceptance: Create with a misspelled cap key and observe invalid_config, and confirm the config schema rejects it.

requirements.statement: A field=$binding reference MUST name the currently bound fact, and its sender MUST be that fact's author or an accepted recipient; a bound ID the sender can read but never received is rejected with reference.
acceptance: Reference a bound fact from a participant that neither authored nor received it and observe reference with the version unchanged.
Reference the same fact from its recipient and observe acceptance.

requirements.statement: The state version MUST count durable records, not transitions: one per accepted fact, host-control record, collection log row and the expiry; entering a state adds nothing and restore verifies the count.
acceptance: Settle a collection's last member with a reply and confirm the version adds the fact and the round close.
Accept presence reports and a fired host trigger and confirm each adds one, while entering the paused state adds nothing.

requirements.statement: An agent's optional local check MUST run the reducer on its verified agent-view projection and discard the candidate state; a local acceptance still requires final room admission.
acceptance: Run the optional checker on a contributor's agent-view projection with a legal reply and confirm accepted.

requirements.statement: Optional per-actor room-event shares MUST default to the room-wide limits; a sender past its event or mention share is refused room_budget and one holding its receipt share retention_limit, while the room-wide limits still apply and the event and mention shares reset with the window.
acceptance: With per-actor shares, a sender past its event share gets room_budget while another sender is accepted; after the window resets it may send again, and a sender holding its receipt share gets retention_limit.
Without per-actor shares, one sender may use the whole room-wide window, and the room-wide limit refuses the next event with room_budget.
A fan-out past the sender's mention share gets room_budget while another sender's event is accepted.
